Order 
This miscellaneous appeal has been filed by the appellants/claimants under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, being aggrieved by the Award dated 08/04/2019 passed by Sixth Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, District- Shivpuri (M.P.) (hereinafter referred to as "the Claims Tribunal") in Claim Case No.100077/2015, on the ground of inadequacy of compensation and seeking enhancement thereof.

entities.text: Sixth Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, District- Shivpuri (M.P.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The date of accident, issue of negligence and the liability of the respondents are not in dispute.
The findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in this regard are not in question.

3. As per the findings of the Claims Tribunal, due to death of Asharam Dhakad in the motor accident, the Claims Tribunal awarded compensation to the tune of Rs.6,10,000/- along with interest from the date of filing of the claim NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:10668 2 MA-3874-2019 petition till realization.

4. Being aggrieved by the impugned award, the appellants/claimants have preferred this appeal on the ground that the learned Claims Tribunal passed the impugned award without proper appreciation of law.
It is contended that the compensation awarded is on the lower side.

The deceased was a healthy person and was engaged in agricultural work and used to earn Rs.10,000/-
Smt. Gayatri vs Tauhid Kha on 31 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33780063/
1 per month.
However, the learned Claims Tribunal failed to consider these aspects and assessed the income of the deceased extremely low.
It is further contended that Claims Tribunal has committed error in not adding future prospects and not awarding reasonable amount of compensation in other conventional heads.
Hence, it is prayed that reasonable amount of compensation may be awarded to the claimants.
5. On the other hand, learned counsels for the Insurance Company supported the impugned award and prayed for rejection of the appeal.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the Claims Tribunal.
7.
O n perusal of record of the Claims Tribunal, it is found that the claimants have utterly failed to adduce any substantial evidence in regard to income of the deceased.

Hence, this Court finds it appropriate to assess the income of the deceased as an unskilled person in view of the law laid down in the cases of Sukhdevi v. Devendra Kumar , ILR 2014 MP 172; Kanwar Devi v. Bansal Roadways ,
2008 ACJ 2182; and National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Renu Devi , (2008) 3 ACC 134 in which it is held that when documentary NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:10668 3 MA-3874-2019 proof of income is lacking, income is to be assessed as per the minimum wages applicable.
Therefore, in considered opinion of this Court, the just and proper amount of the income of the deceased as an unskilled person as per Minimum Wages Act in the present case is Rs.5,845/- per month.
8.

Accordingly, the appellants/claimants are entitled to receive compensation under the following heads:-
 HEAD   Income Rs.5845 x   Future Prospects@ 40% Rs.28,056/
After deducting personal expenses 1/4 Rs.73,647/-
 Multiplier 15 Rs.11,04,7  Other Heads:-
 Loss of Consortium Rs.40,000   Loss of Estate and funeral expenses Rs.30,000/

Total Compensation = Rs.13,34,705/-

2 10.

Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation payable in the present NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:10668 4 MA-3874-2019 case comes to Rs.13,34,705/- as against the sum of Rs.6,10,000/- awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal.
Accordingly, the appellants/claimants are held entitled to an additional compensation of Rs.7,24,705/- over and above the amount already awarded by the Tribunal.
11. In the result, miscellaneous appeal is partly allowed.
The impugned award is modified, and the compensation is enhanced by a sum of Rs.7,24,705/-.
The aforesaid enhanced amount shall carry interest as fixed by Claims Tribunal from the date of deposit of Court fees by the appellants in the present appeal.
The said amount be paid within a period of three months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
Rest of conditions as imposed by learned Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.

12 . In case the enhanced compensation exceeds the valuation of the appeal, the appellants shall deposit the differential Court fee (if not already paid) within a period of one month from today and furnish proof of such payment before the Registry.
Upon compliance, the Registry shall issue the certified copy of this order.
13. In view of the foregoing, the miscellaneous appeal stands partly allowed.
